summary: A struct cast pairs fields by position in the core, because Substrait's struct types carry no names. A frontend that pairs by name resolves the names when it reads the plan: the DuckDB SQL lift and the Ibis producer turn `CAST(s AS STRUCT(...))` into an explicit positional construction, as D54 promises (lifted DuckDB SQL means DuckDB's value). The writer emits a struct cast only when the target keeps the source's names and order. No core option, and the reference makes no pairing choice.
note: Follows DuckDB's fact for the rest: an extra target field becomes a typed NULL, an extra source field is left out, a rename with no name in common is refused (a Binder Error on DuckDB), and nested structs resolve by name at each level. Conditions: S1, one recursive resolver, with structs in lists or maps refused unless the core has an element-wise map there. S2, DuckDB's partial-overlap and case behaviour is probed first. S3, a NULL struct stays NULL. S4, reorder, nested-reorder and NULL tests on DuckDB, Polars and Spark. S5, the refusal stopgap (#2408) lands first. S6, no D-number, and `docs/core-semantics.md` says struct casts pair by position. S7, Improvement lines. The maintainer moved the fix to After 1.0 (#2503), since it needs `Expr.mkStruct` in the core; the design stands for when it is picked up. Ruling 269 names the scope "frontend", which the schema lacks, so the entry is filed under reference-semantics.
